opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jacob Ellison (employee ID E040) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E040.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jacob Ellison (E040) is a full-time Payroll Specialist requesting admin access to Source Code. Under policy, full-time employees max out at write access unless their role owns the system; Source Code is owned by Engineer, not Payroll Specialist. Requested admin exceeds maximum, so recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Jacob Ellison (E040) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors max out at read without advanced training, and never admin. Requested admin exceeds maximum, so recommend granting read.
reason: Jacob Ellison (E040) requests admin access to Source Code. The team notes conflict on employment type: one note says full-time Payroll Specialist (max write, since Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code), while the Security note says contractor with basic security training (max read, never admin). Under either interpretation, admin is above the maximum, so admin cannot be granted. Because the evidence conflicts, I apply the more restrictive applicable maximum: read access for a contractor with basic training. This stays within policy under all readings and grants no more than needed.
